Recall that the equation of an ellipsoid centered at $O$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=1,
$$

and an ellipsoid centered at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}+\frac{(z-{z}_{0})^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=1,
$$

Thus, our equation is an ellipsoid with the following parameters:

$$
({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,-2,0),\,a=3,\,b=\sqrt{7},\,c=2.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadric Surfaces and Cylinders With Alternative Orientations
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of a hyperboloid of two sheets centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=-1.
$$

Thus, a hyperboloid of two sheets centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $x$**-axis** is given by

$$
-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=-1.
$$

Therefore, our equation is a hyperboloid of two sheets whose axis of symmetry is the $x$-axis and $a=b=1,\,c=3.$

questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of an elliptic cylinder whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Thus, an elliptic cylinder whose axis of symmetry is the $x$**-axis** is given by

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, our equation is an elliptic cylinder whose axis of symmetry is the $x$-axis and $b=c=1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadric Surfaces by Completing the Square
questions.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square in the $y$ and $z$ terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}-x-4y-6z-4 & =0 \\ ({y}^{2}-4y)-({z}^{2}+6z)-x-4 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}-4-(z+3)^{2}+9-x-4 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}-(z+3)^{2}+1-x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by rearranging, we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2}-(z+3)^{2}+1-x & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}-(z+3)^{2} & =x-1\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $(1,2,-3).$
